messages:
alex: noticing a p99 latency jump on the eu-dedicated pool starting ~07:40 UTC. throughput okay but tails spiking to ~1.1s.

mira: saw the alert, grabbing profiles. any noisy-tenant tags on those shards?

sam: noisy tenant flag on shard s-44, a bursty recommender workload. KV-cache evictions spiked at the same time.

alex: digging into selector logs — kernel selector switched from quantized-fast -> fp32-lpm at ~07:39 for shortseq paths. suspicious because sequence lengths are sub-32.

mira: that matches. looks like the warmup heuristic misclassified the short-burst distribution. the warmup score dropped and autoswitch jumped to fp32 path which increases per-token latency for short sequences.

jun: incbot created incident INC-2026-1509 severity=high (latency spike affecting customer flows). ops-bot: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-1509 :incident: 

alex: attaching flame snippet from 07:39-07:42:
```
flameprof: kernel_select -> fp32_trt %70
kernel_exec.fp32_trt: 840ms total
kernel_exec.q8x4: 120ms total
kv_cache.eviction: +1800 ops/min
batching.window: default 8ms -> bigger due to fallbacks
```

mira: short term mitigation options: 1) flip feature flag `runtime.selector.prefer_quantized_shortseq=true` 2) throttle tenant s-44 3) route shortseq traffic to low-latency fallback model variant (cheap-llm-8q).

priya: we should also enable `adaptive_warmup.v2=true` on the affected pool — it biases the warmup score to shortseq distributions while it learns. no redeploy needed, runtime flag toggle only.

sam: I'm leaning to quick FF toggle + routing, then enable adaptive_warmup as a longer stabilization. can we measure impact within 2 minutes?

jun: ops ready to flip flags. what are exact flag names and expected immediate delta?

mira: flags: `selector.force_quantized_shortseq=true` (immediate, per-pool) and `adaptive_warmup.v2=true` (per-pool, takes ~1min to converge). expected p99 drop from ~1.1s -> ~220ms for shortseq paths.

ops-bot: @jun executing: runtime-flag-set --pool eu-dedicated --flag selector.force_quantized_shortseq=true --by ops
ops-bot: done (request id r-9c7).

jun: flipped `selector.force_quantized_shortseq` on eu-dedicated at 07:45 UTC.

alex: immediate telemetry: p99 down to 240ms in 30s window, kvcache evictions stabilizing. throughput unaffected. great.

priya: enabling `adaptive_warmup.v2` now so selector stops oscillating once traffic returns to baseline.

ops-bot: @mira executing: runtime-flag-set --pool eu-dedicated --flag adaptive_warmup.v2=true --by ops
ops-bot: done (request id r-9d8).

mira: follow-up action items: 1) postmortem to trace why warmup score dropped (probable shortseq variance detection bug) 2) add regression test for kernel selector under bursty shortseq traffic 3) add alert to detect fast kernel-switch churn (>=3 switches/min) 4) consider hysteresis on selector for dedicated pools.

sam: creating a short-run perf test to reproduce locally with a scaled s-44-like workload and will upload traces.

jun: incident INC-2026-1509 marked resolved at 08:01 UTC after p99 remained stable for 10m.

alex: thanks all. tagging @product-observability for dashboard tweak request (per-route kernel mix). :thumbsup:

incbot: Incident INC-2026-1509 RESOLVED by jun. summary: kernel selector oscillation + KV-cache eviction on noisy tenant caused p99 spike; mitigated via selector force-quantized_shortseq flag + adaptive warmup enable; follow-ups assigned.
